sentences.text: Huehuecanauhtlus was a hadrosauroid dinosaur living during the Late Cretaceous in western Mexico.
This medium-sized hadrosaur reached a length of 6 meters and a mass between 1 and 1.4 metric tons.
Scientists also estimated its height at 2.3 meters and its weight at 1.5 tons.
Its name combines Náhuatl words for ancient and duck.
The correct way to say the name is UEUE-CANA-UHh-TLUS.
Only two fossil individuals of this species are currently known to science.
Angel Alejandro Ramírez-Velasco and colleagues first described and named the genus in 2012.
Both specimens were found at the Barranca Los Bonetes locality in Tuzantla, Michoacán.
Reconstructions suggest this animal lived in the arid paramos that dominated the Cutzamala Formation.
Pathologies observed on the vertebrae and dorsal ribs of the holotype specimen IGM 6253 indicate past health issues.
Excluding Claosaurus, Jeyawati, Levnesovia, Nanyangosaurus, Shuangmiaosaurus, and Telmatosaurus results in a more resolved phylogenetic topology for Huehuecanauhtlus.
Fossils of Huehuecanauhtlus date to the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 85.8 to 83.5 million years ago.
It lived between 86.8 and 84 million years ago in the Cutzamala Formation of Michoacán, Mexico.
